messages:
morgan: Customer PaperSt reporting P99 spikes from AP-SG edge for /v1/generate, started ~08:42 UTC. baseline ~120ms, seeing 800-1200ms. Customer saw sudden region hop in their trace. Link: https://traces.redwood.local/trace/abc123

morgan: Attached snippet from their trace: client -> ap-sg-edge -> eu-west1-proxy -> ap-sg-edge -> redwood-prod-ascend. That eu-west1 hop is unexpected.

devin: Can you paste the raw trace id and a sample request header? also customer id? I want to correlate with our routing logs.

morgan: trace id abc123, customer id paperst-prod-42. Sample req header they sent: `X-Forwarded-For: 103.5.12.8`, `X-Client-Region: ap-sg`.

morgan: Repro steps customer gave: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region: ap-sg" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

incident-bot: [alert] region-affinity-flip detected for ap-sg cluster r-114 at 2026-03-17T08:41:12Z, 7% of connections observed path via eu-west1 before reverting.

priya: Looks like an egress failover to eu-west1 proxy for that AZ. Could be the ap-sg egress proxy reported downstream timeouts and routing shifted to peered eu-west proxy. Checking egress health events now.

devin: I pulled the egress logs for r-114 between 08:40-08:45 UTC: seeing intermittent 502s from upstream (eu-west1-proxy) and then connection resets. snippet: ```
[08:41:10] upstream eu-west1-proxy timed out (110s)
[08:41:11] upstream returned 502
[08:41:12] region fallback triggered -> route to eu-west1-proxy
```

sam: I can repro from our office in SG — I hit the API repeatedly and saw the same pattern: first few requests ~130ms, then a tranche jump to ~900ms and the trace shows the extra eu-west1 hop.

morgan: Customer also sent tcpdump showing SYN->SYN/ACK path: we see their packets reach ap-sg-edge, then connection to eu-west1 over peering link. They said this started after a maintenance window at 08:40.

priya: Two hypotheses: 1) ap-sg egress proxy briefly lost its route to the local compute pool and failed over to peer eu-west; 2) BGP flap/peering issue caused next-hop selection problem. I'll check route updates and peering logs.

devin: For quick mitigation we can pin the customer's traffic to an ap-sg instance (sticky) or add a route exception for paperst-prod-42. Which is faster?

morgan: Customer requests a fix ASAP, sticky routing would be fine as a short-term. We should also provide them repro steps.

priya: I'll push a temporary sticky policy for paperst-prod-42 to prefer local ap-sg egress for 1h. rolling it now.

priya: Done. Policy id: sticky-20260317-p42. Please confirm on your side.

sam: After sticky policy, sam: I ran the same curl loop — p99 back down to ~150ms, no eu-west hop in new traces. confirmed.

devin: Good. I'll open a follow-up to investigate root cause. Capturing: egress proxy timeout -> fallback to peer region -> midflight region hop -> customer P99 spike. Need timeline of maintenance at 08:40 and peering telemetry.

morgan: Customer notified and happy for now, but asked for RCA. Assigning to eng-sre to dig into peering logs and maintenance change.

incident-bot: Created ticket SPT-8492 assigned to eng-sre.

devin: I'll own the RCA. Next steps: collect BGP updates, egress proxy logs, maintenance change details, and packet captures. Anyone with additional telemetry, drop in SPT-8492.

morgan: Thanks — I'll attach the customer's tcpdump and sample traces to the ticket.

priya: Also will check autoscaling events — maybe egress pool scaled down during maintenance and caused transient unhealthy upstreams.

sam: Noted. If we see similar for other tenants, consider alert for cross-region-handoff-rate.

morgan: Closing thread for immediate customer impact. Follow-ups in SPT-8492. :white_check_mark:
